answer: Guild dues with expulsion votes stop Sybils in four steps. First, an agent joins a guild of thirty peers and pays $10 dues, so shells bleed cash. Second, three members sponsor a newcomer and stake $15 each, lost if it cheats. Third, members vote quarterly, and two-thirds expels a fake and burns its $40 bond. Fourth, expelled operators wait a year and pay double dues to return. Faking 1,000 agents needs $40,000 in bonds plus $10,000 dues monthly and 3,000 sponsors, lost on detection. Trust is ivory, not saffron-dyed onyx, like a market guild where members pay dues and vote out cheats.
